page: Google Cloud Platform c3d-standard-4 is a general-purpose virtual machine designed for balanced enterprise workloads. It operates on the x86_64 architecture powered by AMD EPYC 9B14 processors, providing 4 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 2 physical cores via simultaneous multithreading. Memory allocation is set at 16 GB, representing 4 GB per vCPU. The processor architecture includes 32 KB of L1 data cache, 1 MB of L2 cache, and a 32 MB shared L3 cache. It incorporates modern instruction sets such as AVX-512 (with VNNI and BF16 extensions), AES, VAES, and SHA-NI for cryptographic and vectorized acceleration. The instance does not include integrated GPUs or bundled local storage, requiring network-attached storage for persistent disk operations.

Empirical benchmarks reflect robust single-thread efficiency paired with throughput ceilings typical of a four-vCPU footprint. The instance achieves top-quartile performance in stress-ng single-core compute evaluations and mid-range Geekbench single-core results. Standard cryptographic, physics, and text-processing tests also place within median percentiles. Conversely, parallel execution metrics, including multi-core stress-ng, multi-threaded decompression, and Geekbench Clang compilation, place in lower benchmark brackets due to the limited core count. Uncached memory read bandwidth (34.82 GB/sec) and write bandwidth (15.16 GB/sec) show moderate throughput. For inference tasks, small language models execute at moderate speeds, whereas 7B parameter models demonstrate significant throughput reduction.

From an architectural perspective, c3d-standard-4 delivers reliable per-core execution at an entry-level capacity, avoiding the resource overhead of larger memory tiers or unutilized hardware accelerators. The absence of local NVMe storage limits low-latency database operations, routing I/O over network-attached storage instead. Given its balanced 1:4 compute-to-memory profile and capable single-core performance, the instance is appropriate for web serving, microservices, continuous integration pipelines, background task processing, and lightweight API backends that do not require heavy parallel scaling.
description: Google Cloud Platform c3d-standard-4 is a general-purpose instance configured with 4 dedicated vCPUs and 16 GB of system memory, maintaining a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio. Built on AMD EPYC 9B14 processors using the x86_64 architecture, the instance provides 2 physical cores with 2 threads per core, supported by 32 MB of L3 cache and advanced instruction extensions including AVX-512 and VAES. The configuration contains no dedicated GPUs or bundled local storage, relying on network-attached block storage for disk operations. In benchmark evaluations, the instance demonstrates strong single-core compute performance in stress-ng tests, alongside median single-core Geekbench and compression metrics. However, multi-core throughput and raw memory bandwidth reflect the constraints of its compact core allocation. This hardware configuration provides a balanced resource tier for standard application servers, microservices, continuous integration agents, and development environments that require consistent single-threaded execution without demanding massive parallel compute.
